 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR PANDEY  ORAL ORDER 9 13-09-2024 Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Spl. P.P. for the State on I.A. No.01/2023 which has been filed for grant of bail and suspension of sentence.

2. The present appeal has been filed against the judgment of conviction dated 12.01.2022 and order of sentence dated 21.01.2022 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, 6 th cum Special Judge,
POCSO Act, Aurangabad in POCSO Case No. 08 of 2019 arising out of Mahila P.S. Case No. 05 of 2019 whereby the appellant was held guilty for committing the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years alongwith fine of Rs. 5,000/- (five thousand) for the said offence and in default of payment of fine he has to suffer additional three months rigorous imprisonment.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.831 of 2022(9) dt.13-09-2024 3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submits that total period of custody undergone by the appellant is four years and four months.
He further submits that there are several discrepancies in the deposition of prosecution witnesses.

5. Learned A.P.P. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer of bail of the appellant and submits that the earlier bail prayer of the present appellant has already been rejected on merit by this Court on 26.04.2023, statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and her evidence adduced during trial are quite intact and victim can be categorized as sterling witness in the present case.
He further submits that trial court has passed the impugned judgment on due appreciation of evidence adduced by the prosecution witnesses.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.831 of 2022(9)
dt.13-09-2024 case, particularly keeping in view that earlier bail prayer of the appellant has been rejected on merit as well as statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., her evidence adduced during course of trial as well as other material available on record
, I am not inclined to enlarge the appellant on bail.
Accordingly, prayer for the bail of the appellant stands rejected.
8. However, the appellant may renew his prayer for bail after six months, if the appeal is not taken up for hearing.

(Alok Kumar Pandey, J) amitkumar/-
